tasks.desc: Implement the functional-graph counting solution in Python and run the provided samples.
Review edge cases (conflicts, bare/non-bare cycles, spare labels) and finalize the stdin/stdout code.

proposals: Implement the functional-graph counting approach first: validate the S-to-T mapping, count non-fixed source letters, detect nontrivial cycles among present letters, count bare cycles, and check for a buffer via absent letters or duplicate targets.
Build an exhaustive small-alphabet BFS validator for 3 to 5 letters, both with an extra empty letter and with a closed alphabet, to compare exact minima against the formula on all mappings.

Develop a constructive greedy/topological simulator that produces an actual operation sequence for random cases, especially to verify non-bare cycles, buffer creation from duplicate targets, and reuse of one buffer across multiple bare cycles.
If any discrepancy appears, explore an A* or DP search over label-to-target states for reduced alphabets to identify the missing edge case and confirm the lower bound.

Independently derive the result through a token-swapping/blank model to solidify the base-cost lower bound, the bare-cycle extra-cost lower bound, and the buffer availability condition before finalizing the solution.
prev: Implement the functional-graph counting solution in Python: read N, S, T; build target[26] and present[26], rejecting any source letter with two different target letters; compute bad_count, color_freq, and original indegree for bad edges to present targets; use Kahn topological removal to find nontrivial cycles and count a cycle as bare iff every vertex has original indegree 1; set spare = (present_count < 26) or (any color_freq[c] >= 2); print -1 if inconsistent or (bare_cycles > 0 and not spare), otherwise print bad_count + bare_cycles; run the provided samples.
